title: The Eclipse That Never Ends
description:
On 2 August 2027 the Moon's shadow crosses eleven countries and the Sun disappears for six minutes and twenty-three seconds. That is a real event, and it is the longest totality that lands on easily reachable ground until the year 2114.

This video asks what happens if those six minutes never end.

Not the Sun going out. The Moon simply stops, and its shadow stops with it. There is exactly one distance where that works, and it is a distance we already use every day. From there, everything is arithmetic: a Moon nine times wider than the one you know, a circle of permanent night three thousand kilometres across with a hard edge you could step over, and a tide seven hundred and fifty-eight times stronger that never goes out again.

Along the way, two things almost everyone repeats about the 2027 eclipse turn out to be wrong.

The video says out loud which figures are measured, which ones we calculated here and you can check on paper, and which parts are pure speculation.

CHAPTERS
0:00 The shadow has not moved
0:17 What actually happens on 2 August 2027
0:49 Two things you were told
1:29 Now freeze it
1:49 The only distance that works
2:28 A moon nine times too wide
3:02 A circle of permanent night
3:29 The cold that never lifts
3:56 The food stops
4:18 The edge you could step over
4:50 The most valuable ground on Earth
5:30 758 times the tide
6:03 A standing mountain of seawater
6:34 Measured, calculated, guessed
7:23 The day does not change
7:52 The whole scenario in one frame
8:31 Where would you stand?

SOURCES
Solar eclipse of 2 August 2027 - maximum totality 6 min 23 s, path width 258 km, second-longest total eclipse of the 21st century after 22 July 2009, next longer totality on easily accessible land on 3 June 2114:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_eclipse_of_August_2,_2027
The whole world does not go dark - Space.com:
https://www.space.com/stargazing/solar-eclipses/no-the-whole-world-wont-go-dark-on-aug-2-but-a-once-in-a-century-eclipse-is-coming
Geostationary orbit, radius 42,164 km from Earth's centre, altitude 35,786 km:
https://www.rfcafe.com/references/general/geostationary-orbit-calculation.htm
Moon mean distance 384,400 km, mean diameter 3,474 km - NASA Moon fact sheet:
https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/moonfact.html

CALCULATED IN THIS VIDEO, not quoted from a paper:
384,400 / 42,164 = 9.1 times wider. 9.1 cubed = 758 times the tide-raising force. The umbra is roughly the Moon's own diameter, about 3,100 km across.

Visuals are original: illustrated stills and clips generated from our own prompts, plus scenes drawn in code. Narration is AI-generated; the research and the arithmetic are checked by hand.

title: What If An Eclipse Never Ended?
description:
The eclipse began at 10:11. It is now 16:15 and the Sun has not come back. Everyone inside that circle is in permanent night.

There is exactly one distance where the Moon's shadow would hold still over one spot, and we already use it every day.

The full scenario, with the arithmetic shown on screen, is in the long video on this channel.

title: What If The Moon Parked Above You? 758x The Tide
description:
Tide-raising force falls off with the CUBE of distance. Move the Moon in to the geostationary radius, 42,164 km from Earth's centre, and that force goes up about 758 times - and the tide never goes out again.

That 758 is our own arithmetic from the geostationary radius, not a figure lifted from a paper. The working is shown in the long video on this channel.

title: The 2027 Eclipse Is Not What You Were Told
description:
On 2 August 2027 the Sun disappears for 6 minutes and 23 seconds along a band 258 km wide.

Two things almost everyone repeats about it are wrong. The world does not go dark outside that band - outside it, nothing happens at all. And it is not the longest total eclipse of this century: 22 July 2009 was longer.

What it actually is: the longest totality falling on easily reachable ground until 3 June 2114.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_eclipse_of_August_2,_2027
